# Introduction {#sec-intro}

This is a paragraph in **Markdown**: *italics*, **bold**, `code`, and a citation [@wilson2017].
A narrative citation: @marwick2018 argue that a project should be a package.
@sec-data describes the data, @tbl-descr summarises it and @fig-main shows the main result.

# Data and Model {#sec-data}

The example data has `r nrow(dplyr::starwars)` characters. This number is written by R
when the document is rendered: it never goes stale.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descr
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive statistics"
#| echo: false
sw <- dplyr::starwars
vars <- c(Height = "height", Mass = "mass", `Birth year` = "birth_year")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Variable = names(vars),
  N    = sapply(vars, \(v) sum(!is.na(sw[[v]]))),
  Mean = sapply(vars, \(v) mean(sw[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)),
  SD   = sapply(vars, \(v) sd(sw[[v]], na.rm = TRUE))
), digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)
```

We estimate @eq-main by OLS.

$$
Y_i = \alpha + \beta X_i + \varepsilon_i
$$ {#eq-main}

# Results {#sec-results}

```{r}
#| label: fig-main
#| fig-cap: "Taller characters are heavier"
#| echo: false
sw <- subset(sw, mass < 1000)
plot(mass ~ height, data = sw, pch = 19, xlab = "Height (cm)", ylab = "Mass (kg)")
abline(lm(mass ~ height, data = sw))
```

One more centimetre is associated with `r round(coef(lm(mass ~ height, data = sw))[2], 2)` kg more.
